sections.content:
This course includes stuff that is in COMP1023(basically the powerpoints are the same),making it a bridging course for students who have taken COMP1021 but need to proceed  to other higher-level COMP requirements. If you have not studied ICT in high school, you can still try on COMP1023 directly as I think you'll learn things more efficiently. However if you're not too confident in directly taking a hard computer course, taking COMP1021 then COMP1028 can allow you to have a more gentle introduction to programming, as COMP1021 doesn't include Numpy and Pandas, which makes it less Mathematically heavy(some matrix concept is needed in COMP1023'sNumpy and Pandas) . However, in exchange of that, you have to learn Turtle which is not in COMP1023, basically focuses more on iterations and drawing stuff on the screen by programming. Eventually deciding whether you should take COMP1021+COMP1028 combo or directly taking COMP1023 is determined by whether you have some matrix concept or not(even though COMP1028 does have the same material as COMP1023, but considering this is in winter semester, you can spend some time to learn matrix by yourself), also if you hate Turtle then just choose COMP1023 instead.
1st week
Lecture 1: Introduction---basic components of computer
Lecture 2: Basic Programmign Language elements
Lecture 3: Collection type

2nd week
Lecture 4: Functions
Lecture 5: Recursions
Lecture 6: Modules package libraries

3rd week
Lecture 7: Object Oriented Programming
Lecture 8: NumPy

4th week
Lecture 9: Pandas
Lecture 10: Matplotlib
sections.teaching: This is a self-study course, material are put in Canvas and you are expected to self study 73-90 pages of notes a week, but I find it quite comfortable as I can study things on my own pace. Additionally, the notes are structured well, easy to follow the content. Also it's in Winter Semester in which considering its short period of time, you won't really take much courses, so you don't need to worry much about other subjects. All you need to do is to focus on this course and also enjoy your time during the holiday without being too detach from or stressed  by the academic stuff.

sections.workload: Considering it's a 1-credit course, the workload is quite large, but definitely not as much as an average 3 credit course. 70+pages read within a week and 4 assignments hand in consecutively in 4 weeks(each week 1 assignment). Some of them are harder than others, but 2 of them are actually quite short.
